name: The Oak Tree
address: The Oak Tree, Newtown, Ferns, Co. Wexford
questions: Is there any shower or bath on the kitchen level? Could the guest WC (1.71 × 1.83 m) or the utility (3.78 × 1.83 m) become a shower room, so the 7.07 × 5.43 m living area works as a bedroom for older parents without using the stairs?
How many steps are on the internal stair between the kitchen level and the bedroom level, and on the external steps up to the front door? Is there a level route from the car to the front door?
Is the house on mains water or a private well, and is drainage a septic tank or a treatment unit (age and certificate)? What heats the house, and how old is the boiler?
What drives the D1 rating (245.96 kWh/m²/yr): wall and attic insulation, windows, boiler? Have any upgrades been costed?

Which boundaries are fenced, and could the front lawn be closed off from the road for two dogs? What is the large building with the yard about 90 m south-west along the road, and has the asking price changed since April?

ai.why: A characterful 198 m² house at €450k, set back from a quiet road. But it is split-level with stairs everywhere, has only two bathrooms, both up a 12–13 step stair, and the ED is 40–45 minutes away.

electricity.detail: Connected; an occupied house with an electric oven, though the listing doesn't state the supply.

water.detail: Not stated; a rural house 2 km north of Ferns may be on a private well or group scheme. Ask.

sewer.detail: Not stated; almost certainly a septic tank or treatment unit outside the village. Ask its age and for a certificate.

internet.detail: Fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband: 102 Mb full fibre'); the listing doesn't mention broadband. Provider not confirmed; rural north Wexford is NBI territory.
internet.speed: ~100 Mb+ (up to 1 Gb on full fibre plans)

groundFloorBedroom.detail: The 7.07 × 5.43 m living area is on the drive level, on the same floor as the kitchen and across the hall from it (two steps up to the dining end), with a guest WC and patio doors. But that level has no shower or bath: every bathroom is up a straight 12–13 step stair.

type: Detached split-level house with an attached workshop and a detached garage
bedsNote: The house is built into a slope. The front door is about 8 external steps up from the drive and opens onto the bedroom level: master (5.37 × 3.64 m, walk-in wardrobe, en suite) up a further 3 steps, bedroom 2 (2.77 × 4.86 m), bedroom 1 (2.85 × 2.29 m, a single), the family bathroom, the sitting room and the sunroom. A straight 12–13 step stair goes down to the drive level: kitchen-dining, utility, guest WC and the 7.07 × 5.43 m living area offered as a 4th bedroom or office. The floor plans call the bedroom level 'ground' and the kitchen level 'first'; the brochure text and the photos show the kitchen level is the lower one. '3 baths' counts the guest WC.
heating: Not stated; open fire in the sitting room and a solid-fuel stove in the kitchen. The hob runs on gas (probably bottled LPG).
tagline: A 198 m² split-level 4-bed with a beamed sunroom and open fire, on 0.79 acres of hedged gardens with rural views, about 2 km north of Ferns village.

pros.detail: €2,273/m² and about €4,500 stamp duty. It has been listed since 9 April 2026 (about six months, 8,991 Daft views), which leaves room to negotiate.

Sunroom 3.94 × 5.14 m with a vaulted, beamed timber ceiling and doors to a balcony; sitting room 5.26 × 3.56 m with an open stone fireplace and a bay window; kitchen-dining 7.69 × 3.68 m with a stove.

pros.text: A big room level with the kitchen
pros.detail: The 7.07 × 5.43 m living area shares the drive level with the kitchen, utility and guest WC, and opens to the patio and tarmac yard at grade: a step-free route from the car, but see the bathroom con.

pros.text: 0.79 acres, set back from a quiet road
pros.detail: On the L1014 local road, about 35 m back behind tall hedges, with tillage fields behind. The Aug 2024 Esri image shows no industry; the nearest farmyards are about 400 m east-north-east and 500 m south.

pros.text: GP, shop and schools 2–3 km away
pros.detail: Ferns Health Centre, Centra and the Ferns bus stop are about 2.2 km away; Naomh Maodhog NS (301 pupils) is 2.1 km and St Edan's NS 2.8 km, per Daft.

pros.text: Workshop, garage and a big yard
pros.detail: An attached 5.5 × 4 m workshop, a detached 7.4 × 4.7 m garage, a large tarmac drive and a hot tub.
BuyerIQ lists 102 Mb full fibre at the address.

cons.detail: The front door is about 8 external steps up. A straight stair of 12–13 steps joins the kitchen level to the bedrooms, the sitting room and the only bath and shower, and the master is 3 more steps up. Fitting a shower room on the kitchen level would cost roughly €8–15k (rough).
245.96 kWh/m²/yr, and the heating system isn't stated. Bringing it to about B2 would cost roughly €30–60k (rough), with grants.

cons.text: Dublin train is a drive and about 2 hours
cons.detail: Gorey and Enniscorthy stations are each about 15 km away. The Rosslare–Dublin line runs 5 trains each weekday, about 1h45–2h to Connolly.
Wexford General (all ages) is about 31 km straight-line, roughly 42 km by road.
Bedroom 1 is 2.85 × 2.29 m (6.5 m²), so the 'three doubles' are really two doubles and a single. Room for six depends on giving up the second living room.

It is one of about seven houses along the road, with neighbours about 20–25 m away on each side. The front lawn faces the road behind a low wall, and a large building with a big yard about 90 m south-west is of unknown use.
BuyerIQ shows 1 critical and 6 high-priority findings (fixes €20.8k–28k, hidden), and 5 planning applications within 1 km including an active build. Water, sewer and heating aren't stated.
